alterations.description: Added a tablet in Hindi stating the film broadly follows the legend of the 18th-century poet Isardaan, but with changes for dramatic effect.
Shot of bust-jerking by the dancer Vidvadhari and the reaction of Matndin.
Shot of Bhairav's vulgar gesture of eating flowers from his garland.
Shot of Tsardaan’s skeleton as visualized by Vidyudhari.
The word “Vcshya” from Manjula’s dialogue addressed to Madhav.
Visuals of a girl being accosted, from the song beginning with the words “Aaj kaalchya duniyc maazi”.
Credit titles along with the song lines as background music at places.
From the dialogue of Sunil (disguised as Pathan) his remarks “Bulbule Hindustan” referring to Shobhna and his reference to Shobhna being an addition to his harem of three wives.
Dialogue in the operation theatre regarding the torch not being available when the lights are put off by the villain.
Distorted recitation of Shlokas in the marriage ceremony and dialogue suggesting the pundit started the wedding ceremony before the auspicious time at the villain's instance.
Considerably reduced the scene of Sunil’s father anticipating his death, particularly the loud chanting associated with a Hindu funeral.
The scene of Kishore making his father dance with him.
From song beginning with the words “Ek paisa ki hai savaal jiye tero bachhe maayee" to a flash, shots of collective begging by children moving around in the streets.
In the song-dance sequence "Nat khat pare hat" shots of bust-shaking by the principal dancer.

Close-up of the bust of the dancer before start of the dance “Naina re dekho un ke nain”; shot of the emphasised bust of the dancer as she lifts up her arms while bending backwards; and shots of shaking of bust.
From the song-dance sequence “Chain kahan, aaram kahan" shot of bust-shaking by the female dancer while sitting.
From the song-dance sequence “More ruthe balam ghar aa" shots of bust-shaking by the dancer while sitting.

In the song-dance sequence shots of the two dancers in which they move their stomach, hips and thighs indecently and shots in which the tights worn by them under their transparent shalwars give the impression of nudity.
Shot of Sultan Allaudin doing the "sajdah" while saluting the ashes of Maharani Padmini.
Tablet at the beginning of the film dedicated to forces of rational thought opposed to violence and seeking to strengthen the government's task of tackling pressing national problems.
Substantially reduced the visuals of protests.
The sound of thunder in the sequence showing the policemen.
The underlined words from the line: “But beforo the cup of patience is spilled, before violent retaliation begins to arouse the devil in man, before caution is thrown to the winds”.
The following lines: “Said the poet: When the world is full of paddy, When the world is full of Wheat, Why should there be thousands Who have no food to eat?”
The close-up of the sergeant.
The scene of Kishore making his father dance with him.
From song beginning with the words “Ek paisa ki hai savaal jiye tero bachhe maayee" to a flash, shots of collective begging by children moving around in the streets.
In the song-dance sequence "Nat khat pare hat" shots of bust-shaking by the principal dancer.

Close-up of the bust of the dancer before start of the dance “Naina re dekho un ke nain”; shot of the emphasised bust of the dancer as she lifts up her arms while bending backwards; and shots of shaking of bust.

From the song-dance sequence “More ruthe balam ghar aa" shots of bust-shaking by the dancer while sitting.

Shot of Sultan Allaudin doing the "sajdah" while saluting the ashes of Maharani Padmini.
The bare back view of Lynn after Bill snatches her bra.
The near views of the bust of Tuyet when she is wearing a wet slip.
Captain Dee’s talk to Rice as follows: "By which Americans always mean ballot boxes. We cannot eat ballot boxes" as also, "The Asian mind is different."
The semi-nude view of Tuyet as she turns to Bill to kiss him.
The passionate kissing between Emily and Charles.
The semi-nude shots of the girl in Bus's room.
The shot of a semi-nude girl in Bus's room.
Various shots.
The shots of Balu throwing paper rolls at a girl.
The sound of whistling by the boys in the college premises.
The shot of Govindani pointing to the caste mark of the office boy before saying that the salary would be Rs. 300.
The actual shot of the boy removing the car wheel hub and also his reply when questioned.
Song 3 — Delete the entire picturisation of the song. (No objection to the text of the song) (Redited picturisation approved).
Reduce the scene of gang chief having drink before Kamala, delete the close shot of visuals of trade name of a drink.
Delete the near views of Parimala in jeans with emphasised bust while she is talking to Chandra.
Delete the scene of bottles, men and women, also deleting a man having drink and offering to his son.

Song 5— Delete close shots of the female dancer when she is single and also with others. From text, delete verse ‘Davani Potta. . . .Kekkudhillai’. Also delete the shot where boys lift the girls towards the end of the song.
